problem: Write the equation of the hyperbola $2{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}=14$ in standard form.

feedback.problem:
The equation of the hyperbola $20{y}^{2}-15{x}^{2}=120$ in standard form is{{field-1}}
$=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{y}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

Therefore, to write the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to divide both sides of the equation by $120$ and then simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}20{y}^{2}-15{x}^{2} & =120 \\ \frac{20{y}^{2}}{120}-\frac{15{x}^{2}}{120} & =\frac{120}{120} \\ \frac{{y}^{2}}{6}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{8} & =1\end{aligned}
$$
